explanation: Texas court string-cites Grovey to hold no governmental action in the union-shop statute; Smith v. Allwright (1944) overruled Grovey on exactly its state-action holding (own knowledge; no excerpt). No negative history noted; unrelated litigation.

Minnesota court cites McGinnis as authority sustaining employer criminal liability for a bartender's unauthorized sale; McCance (1892) overruled McGinnis on that point (own recollection; no excerpt). No acknowledgment; different litigation.

D.C. Circuit reversed the PSRO-is-an-agency holding (own knowledge), but Byers cites the district decision only as a contrast in a footnote, distinguishing the corporate defendants from the PSRO; it is not relied on for the holding.

Logsdon relies on Brenner for the definition of joint tort liability (concert, same character of care); Meyer overruled only syllabus paragraph three, a different point (verdict against one joint defendant, per my recollection), so the negation is off point.

O'Hara cites the district decision in Moore v. Bonner as authority that the administrative hearing satisfied collateral-estoppel prerequisites; the Fourth Circuit had reversed it outright in 1982 on administrative preclusion. No subsequent history noted; unrelated litigation.

Benson cites the civil appeals Wilson decision for dishonesty usually being a jury question; Texas Supreme Court reversed it in 1970 as to the principal defendants, on the dishonesty determination (own recollection; no excerpt). No history noted; different litigation.

Craig cites Grasser as supporting authority that a common-law claim lies for serving a known alcoholic; Jackson v. PKM (1988) overruled that holding, finding the dram shop act exclusive (own knowledge). No acknowledgment; different litigation.
